In light of recent happenings, it's worth remembering that archiving pages can be of importance down the road, when it comes to compiling evidence. What tipped me off was a post that's probably insignificant in the grand scheme of things. I looked up both the original account and the account that he was retweeting. The former appears to have deleted his post, but his recent posting history strongly suggests the post existed at one point. The latter's account was suspended. With neither tweet in the image archived, there is no absolute proof of either happening, going by the screenshot alone.

This, of course, is a rather minor example of the importance of archiving, but as of writing this post, it's the first post that shows up in v/whatever. Once you get into meatier pieces of evidence, such as the social media presence of the shooter, archiving becomes more important. In short, if you're going to share information of this nature, use an archival site like archive.is, and either provide an archive link, or put said link in an image, if you choose to share an image.
